questions.question: Does your organization have a Board-approved digital health strategy aligned with Pakistan's National Health Vision?

levelDescriptions.1: No digital health strategy exists
levelDescriptions.2: Informal IT plans exist but not Board-adopted
levelDescriptions.3: Written strategy exists but only partially implemented
levelDescriptions.4: Board-approved strategy with KPIs tracked quarterly
levelDescriptions.5: Dynamic strategy integrated with UHC goals, informed by AI-driven insights

questions.question: What percentage of your annual operating budget is allocated to health analytics and digital transformation?

levelDescriptions.1: No dedicated budget for analytics or digital health
levelDescriptions.2: Less than 1% allocated, ad-hoc funding only
levelDescriptions.3: 1-3% allocated with annual budget line item
levelDescriptions.4: 3-6% allocated with multi-year investment roadmap
levelDescriptions.5: Over 6% allocated with ROI tracking and value-based reinvestment

questions.question: Is there a formal change management framework for digital transformation initiatives?

levelDescriptions.1: No change management process; changes are reactive
levelDescriptions.2: Ad-hoc communication when new systems are introduced
levelDescriptions.3: Basic change management with training sessions for major rollouts
levelDescriptions.4: Structured framework (e.g., ADKAR) with dedicated change champions per department
levelDescriptions.5: Enterprise-wide change management culture with continuous feedback loops and adoption metrics

questions.question: Does your organization employ dedicated health informatics professionals?

levelDescriptions.1: No health informatics roles exist; IT staff handle all tasks
levelDescriptions.2: One or two IT staff have partial informatics responsibilities
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated health informatics unit with 2-4 professionals
levelDescriptions.4: Full informatics department with specialized roles (clinical, technical, research)
levelDescriptions.5: Center of excellence with certified informaticists, fellowship programs, and research output

questions.question: Are data scientists or biostatisticians on staff to support clinical analytics?

levelDescriptions.1: No data science capability exists in-house
levelDescriptions.2: Occasional outsourced analytics projects
levelDescriptions.3: 1-2 data analysts performing descriptive reporting
levelDescriptions.4: Dedicated data science team with predictive modeling capabilities
levelDescriptions.5: Multi-disciplinary analytics team with PhD-level scientists, ML engineers, and clinical domain experts

questions.question: Are clinical informaticist roles established to bridge clinical practice and technology?

levelDescriptions.1: No clinical informaticist roles; clinicians and IT operate in silos
levelDescriptions.2: A few clinicians informally consult on IT decisions
levelDescriptions.3: Designated physician or nurse champions for specific systems (e.g., EMR)
levelDescriptions.4: Formal Clinical Informatics Officer (CMIO/CNIO) role with governance authority
levelDescriptions.5: Clinical informatics integrated into all departments with dual-trained professionals driving evidence-based digital care

questions.question: Is ICD-10 coding used consistently for all diagnoses across the organization?

levelDescriptions.1: No standardized coding; free-text diagnoses only
levelDescriptions.2: ICD-10 used in billing but not clinical records
levelDescriptions.3: ICD-10 coded for inpatient discharges; outpatient partially covered
levelDescriptions.4: ICD-10 coded across all encounters with trained coders and quality audits
levelDescriptions.5: ICD-10 with ICD-11 transition roadmap, SNOMED-CT mapping, and automated NLP-assisted coding

questions.question: Is a Master Patient Index (MPI) implemented to uniquely identify patients across systems?

levelDescriptions.1: No unique patient identifier; duplicate records are common
levelDescriptions.2: Manual ID assignment with frequent duplicates across departments
levelDescriptions.3: Single MPI within the main hospital system but not across branches
levelDescriptions.4: Enterprise MPI with deterministic and probabilistic matching across all facilities
levelDescriptions.5: National Health ID integrated MPI with real-time deduplication and cross-organizational linkage

questions.question: Are formal data sharing agreements in place with referring facilities, labs, or public health authorities?

levelDescriptions.1: No data sharing agreements; data stays within the facility
levelDescriptions.2: Informal data exchange via email or paper for specific cases
levelDescriptions.3: Bilateral agreements with 1-2 partners (e.g., a reference lab)
levelDescriptions.4: Standardized data sharing agreements with multiple partners and defined security protocols
levelDescriptions.5: Participation in regional/national Health Information Exchange with automated, consent-based data sharing

questions.question: Is an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system deployed for clinical documentation?

levelDescriptions.1: Fully paper-based records; no EMR in use
levelDescriptions.2: Basic EMR in 1-2 departments (e.g., registration or pharmacy)
levelDescriptions.3: EMR covers major clinical departments but paper processes remain
levelDescriptions.4: Comprehensive EMR across all departments with CPOE and clinical decision support
levelDescriptions.5: Fully integrated EMR with AI-assisted documentation, voice input, and real-time clinical intelligence

questions.question: Are laboratory and pharmacy systems integrated with the core clinical system?

levelDescriptions.1: Lab and pharmacy operate standalone systems with manual result entry
levelDescriptions.2: One-way data feed from lab or pharmacy to EMR (e.g., PDF reports)
levelDescriptions.3: Bidirectional integration for lab orders and results; pharmacy partially integrated
levelDescriptions.4: Full LIS/PIS integration with barcode verification, auto-dispensing alerts, and order tracking
levelDescriptions.5: Closed-loop medication and lab management with real-time analytics, drug interaction checks, and smart inventory

questions.question: Is telemedicine infrastructure available for remote consultations and follow-ups?

levelDescriptions.1: No telemedicine capability; all consultations are in-person
levelDescriptions.2: Ad-hoc video calls via consumer apps (WhatsApp, Zoom) for select cases
levelDescriptions.3: Dedicated telemedicine platform for outpatient follow-ups with scheduling
levelDescriptions.4: Integrated telehealth with EMR documentation, e-prescribing, and specialist tele-consults
levelDescriptions.5: Omni-channel virtual care (video, chat, RPM devices) with AI triage, multilingual support, and rural outreach

questions.question: Do department heads have access to clinical and operational dashboards?

levelDescriptions.1: No dashboards; reporting is via ad-hoc spreadsheets or verbal updates
levelDescriptions.2: Monthly static reports generated manually by IT for select departments
levelDescriptions.3: Basic dashboards (bed occupancy, OPD volumes) available but not widely used
levelDescriptions.4: Interactive BI dashboards per department with drill-down, updated daily or in real-time
levelDescriptions.5: Self-service analytics platform with role-based dashboards, anomaly alerts, and embedded AI recommendations

questions.question: Are predictive analytics models used for clinical or operational decision-making?

levelDescriptions.1: No predictive analytics; all decisions based on historical data or intuition
levelDescriptions.2: Awareness of predictive analytics but no models deployed
levelDescriptions.3: Pilot predictive model in one area (e.g., readmission risk or demand forecasting)
levelDescriptions.4: Multiple validated predictive models in production (sepsis, mortality, bed demand)
levelDescriptions.5: Enterprise-wide predictive and prescriptive analytics with real-time clinical decision support at the point of care

questions.question: Are AI or machine learning models deployed in any clinical or operational workflow?

levelDescriptions.1: No AI/ML usage in any workflow
levelDescriptions.2: Exploring AI use cases; no deployments yet
levelDescriptions.3: One AI tool in limited use (e.g., radiology AI for chest X-rays)
levelDescriptions.4: Multiple AI models in production with clinical validation and monitoring frameworks
levelDescriptions.5: AI-native operations with continuous learning models, explainability dashboards, and regulatory compliance (e.g., DRAP AI guidelines)

questions.question: Do laboratory results automatically flow into the patient's electronic record?

levelDescriptions.1: Lab results are printed and manually filed in paper charts
levelDescriptions.2: Lab results are scanned or attached as PDFs in the EMR
levelDescriptions.3: Structured lab results auto-populate in EMR for most tests
levelDescriptions.4: Full auto-flow with discrete data, critical value alerts, and trending graphs
levelDescriptions.5: Real-time streaming of all diagnostic results with AI-interpreted summaries and clinical pathway triggers

questions.question: Are FHIR-compliant API endpoints available for external system integration?

levelDescriptions.1: No APIs; all integrations are file-based or manual
levelDescriptions.2: Proprietary APIs for 1-2 integrations (e.g., lab vendor interface)
levelDescriptions.3: HL7 v2 messaging for core integrations; FHIR awareness but no endpoints
levelDescriptions.4: FHIR R4 endpoints for key resources (Patient, Observation, Encounter) with OAuth2 security
levelDescriptions.5: Full FHIR R4/R5 API surface with SMART-on-FHIR apps, bulk data export, and developer portal

questions.question: Does your facility participate in any Health Information Exchange (HIE) network?

levelDescriptions.1: No participation in any data exchange network
levelDescriptions.2: Aware of HIE initiatives but not connected
levelDescriptions.3: Connected to one exchange (e.g., provincial disease surveillance reporting)
levelDescriptions.4: Active participation in regional HIE with bidirectional data exchange
levelDescriptions.5: Multi-network HIE participation (national, regional, cross-border) with real-time event notifications and patient consent management

questions.question: Can patients access their health records through a patient portal or app?

levelDescriptions.1: No patient-facing digital access to records
levelDescriptions.2: Patients can request records via email or front desk
levelDescriptions.3: Basic patient portal with visit summaries and lab results (view-only)
levelDescriptions.4: Full-featured portal with records, messaging, medication lists, and care plans
levelDescriptions.5: Personalized health hub with AI health insights, wearable data integration, and family/caregiver access

questions.question: Are mHealth applications deployed for patient education, monitoring, or chronic disease management?

levelDescriptions.1: No mobile health applications in use
levelDescriptions.2: General health education content shared via social media channels
levelDescriptions.3: One mHealth app deployed (e.g., appointment reminders via SMS)
levelDescriptions.4: Multiple mHealth tools for chronic disease management, medication adherence, and remote monitoring
levelDescriptions.5: Comprehensive mHealth ecosystem with AI chatbots, multilingual support (Urdu, Sindhi, Pashto), and community health worker integration

questions.question: Can patients book appointments digitally (online, app, or WhatsApp)?

levelDescriptions.1: Appointments only via walk-in or phone call
levelDescriptions.2: Phone-based booking with manual entry into scheduling system
levelDescriptions.3: Online booking available but limited to select departments or doctors
levelDescriptions.4: Full digital booking across all services with automated reminders and waitlist management
levelDescriptions.5: AI-optimized scheduling with real-time slot availability, dynamic capacity management, and multi-channel booking (web, app, WhatsApp, IVR)

questions.question: Can your organization measure and report 30-day readmission rates accurately?

levelDescriptions.1: Readmission rates are not tracked
levelDescriptions.2: Manual tracking for select units (e.g., cardiology) upon request
levelDescriptions.3: Automated readmission tracking from EMR data for inpatient discharges
levelDescriptions.4: Real-time readmission dashboards by diagnosis, department, and physician with root cause analysis
levelDescriptions.5: Predictive readmission risk scoring at discharge with automated intervention workflows and outcome tracking

questions.question: Does your organization benchmark clinical outcomes against national or international standards?

levelDescriptions.1: No clinical outcome benchmarking performed
levelDescriptions.2: Internal trend analysis for a few indicators (e.g., mortality rate)
levelDescriptions.3: Benchmarking against national averages for key indicators
levelDescriptions.4: Systematic benchmarking against regional and international peers with published quality reports
levelDescriptions.5: Participation in global quality registries (e.g., ICHOM, JCI benchmarks) with continuous improvement cycles and public transparency

questions.question: Does your organization conduct cost-effectiveness analysis for clinical programs and digital investments?

levelDescriptions.1: No cost-effectiveness analysis capability
levelDescriptions.2: Basic cost tracking at department level without linking to outcomes
levelDescriptions.3: Cost-per-case analysis for select DRGs or procedures
levelDescriptions.4: Systematic cost-effectiveness analysis for all major clinical programs and IT investments with ROI reporting
levelDescriptions.5: Value-based care analytics with total cost of care modeling, QALY calculations, and real-time financial-clinical correlation dashboards

metadata.targetAudience: CTO, Medical Director, Health IT Lead
